The exposure observable commutes ACTIVE_g, though it need not commute the terminal loss/reset. Thus all extra product/tilt gains and anticommutators lie in the **full** ACTIVE corner and are bounded by C ACTIVE_g. A no-move terminal is allowed to change controller availability. No fictitious zero-cost controller action or retained-terminal-energy payment is needed.

The entry split charges false WANT, malformed W/ownership and active overlapping neighbors explicitly. A two-by-two Young estimate pays dirty diagonals and clean/dirty derivative cross blocks by debt and a quadratic clean source; cleanup-created cross blocks are not discarded. With zeta=`c_z lambda t`, beta_A=`C_b lambda t`, delta=`C_d sqrt(lambda)t`, c_z small, C_b large and lambda sufficiently small, the actual full nominal first-order inequality has negative coefficient of order lambda t on

`B_cov=sum_h(F_h a_h+ACTIVE_h)+sum_v R_v`,

## 7. Noncommuting proof circuit: exact order and boundary comparison

The proof compresses **each generator** Xi to P0 before defining Y0, S0 and W0. It then kills at the different spectral projector `P1=1_(W0<=exp(aN))` within P0. The full extension F=W0+(I-P0) commutes P1 exactly. No finite-depth local Taylor theorem is applied to the nonlocal compressed circuit.

I checked the actual receiving constants against the abstract proof. For every fixed integer m the ordered identity for `A0^m W0^-m`, with A0=P0 V_c P0, gives

`V0^(2m)<=exp([2m c_t t+C_m delta]N)W0^(2m)`.

This is a derived norm/congruence inequality; it is not an arbitrary Loewner inequality raised to a power. Weighted compression is harmless because P0 commutes E and A. Each fixed-order weighted local Xi norm is uniform in t,lambda, so the constants required by this identity remain fixed as the proof parameters are made small.

The boundary comparison must keep the entire block-diagonal Xi operator `P0 Xi P0+Q0 Xi Q0`. Its difference from Xi is then genuinely supported on the high-energy crossing strip on both sides. The one-gate Duhamel formula, followed by O(N)-gate telescoping, has a strip projector acting on every relevant partial word. The higher moments on P1 bound that partial-word tail, including fixed local insertions and fixed powers of A. Remaining coarse norms cost only exp(CN) with C independent of m. Fixing m sufficiently large first, then t and delta sufficiently small, makes all these errors exponentially small.

This gives bilinear operator-norm bounds on `P1 U*(F-W)V P1` for every bounded system leg, not only one-state expectation bounds. Complete physical Hamiltonian, gain and loss terms are all covered. The finite system-leg cb expansion handles the newly explicit noise class with its weighted O(N) sum. A trace-norm comparison of `S rho S*` with `S0 rho S0*` follows with the same reference-uniform budget. The latter state is exactly P0-supported, so only at this point may D>=E be used.

All receiving premises of the separately completed two-basin theorem are therefore earned by the actual instance. The previously identified noncommuting killed-compression obstruction is repaired, not dismissed by raw potential comparability or the entropy identity alone.
